d.g: Especially of a series of ideas, letters, words, etc.: intended to help in remembering.
Of or relating to mnemonics (“the study of techniques for remembering anything more easily”).
Something (especially a series of ideas, letters, words, etc.) used to help in remembering a thing; a memory aid.

mnemonic.e: Borrowed from Late Latin mnemonicus or its etymon Ancient Greek μνημονῐκός (mnēmonĭkós, “pertaining to memory or remembrance, memorial”) + English -ic (suffix meaning ‘of or pertaining to’ forming adjectives). …

mnemotechnic.e: English mnemo- English technic English mnemotechnic From mnemo- + technic.

mnemonics.e: From Ancient Greek μνημονικά (mnēmoniká, “mnemonics”), plural of μνημονικόν (mnēmonikón, “mnemonics”), neuter of μνημονικός (mnēmonikós, “mnemonic”); see mnemonic.

d.g: Someone able to perform feats of memory, especially by using mnemonic techniques.
